For potentials with $V(0)=0$, $\nabla V(0)=0$, and $I\le\nabla^2V\le2I$, the least worst-case query budget achieving total-variation error at most $1/10$ is at most $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and at least $c\log d$ eventually. statements.name: thm:main
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
In the oracle model above, for every \(\varepsilon>0\)
there is \(C_\varepsilon<\infty\) such that
\[
                  Q(d)\le C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon
                  \qquad(d\ge2).
\]
There are also absolute constants \(c>0\) and \(d_0\)
such that
\[
                  Q(d)\ge c\log d\qquad(d\ge d_0).
\]
The lower bound applies to arbitrary randomized adaptive
first-order algorithms. In particular, \(\gamma_*=0\).
